title: Containment Configuration Guide for Private Access

blocks.text: This configuration guide provides information on prerequisites and how to integrate Zscaler Deception with Private Access (ZPA) to contain and isolate detected attackers.
Before you configure the containment integration, ensure that you have:

blocks.item: Signed in to the Zscaler Admin Console and configured an IdP for single sign-on (SSO) in Private Access.
Obtained the Private Access tenant ID from the Zscaler Admin Console (Administration > Account Management > Private Access Tenant).

blocks.heading: Configuring Containment Integration with Private Access

blocks.text: Follow these steps to configure containment integration with Private Access:

blocks.item: Step 1: Configure the Containment Integration Between Deception and Private Access
In Zscaler Deception Admin Portal, go to Orchestrate > Containment.
In the table, locate Zscaler Private Access and click the Edit icon.
See image.
In the Zscaler Private Access configuration window:
Enabled: Select to enable containment.
Customer ID: Verify if the customer ID matches the Private Access tenant ID that you obtained from the Zscaler Admin Console.
IdP: Select all IdPs that you want to integrate.
If SCIM Sync or SCIM Attributes for Policy are disabled in the IdP, enter the SAML attribute name.
See image.
Click Save.
After the configuration is saved, click Test to verify network connectivity between the Deception Admin Portal and Private Access.

If Authentication Service is enabled for your organization, the Authentication Service IdP is displayed automatically in the Zscaler Private Access configuration window. This cannot be edited or deleted.
If a user is contained with Private Access, real apps become inaccessible and only app decoys remain accessible.
Step 2: Configure Orchestration Rule or Take Action to Contain Detected Attackers
You can contain detected attackers automatically by creating an orchestrated rule or manually by taking action from the Investigate page.
Create a rule.
Go to Orchestrate > Rule.
Click Add Rule.
See image.
In the Rule Details window:
Enter the name of the rule.
Select Enabled.
Create a rule using queries and conditions.
See image.
Under Respond, enable Zscaler Private Access.
See image.
Click Save.
The attacker is contained by Private Access based on the conditions configured when the rule is triggered.
Take action from the Investigate page.
On the Investigate page, click an attack icon on the alert graph.
The attacker details pane opens.
See image.
Click Actions.
A list of actions that you can take to remediate the threat appears.
Click the Zscaler drop-down menu, and then select Contain with Zscaler Private Access.
See image.
In the confirmation window, click OK.

blocks.text: After containing the detected attackers, you can view the details of the attacker.
